entries.name: Trust region policy optimization
entries.title: Trust Region Policy Optimization
entries.definition: A policy-optimization method that optimizes a surrogate objective while constraining the change in policy by a trust region based on Kullback–Leibler divergence.
entries.mechanism: The practical method estimates a surrogate objective from sampled trajectories and constrains the average divergence from the old policy, using an approximate constrained update rather than evaluating a maximum-divergence constraint at every state.
entries.locator: Sections 4–6, PDF pp. 3–5; equations 12–15 and practical-approximation discussion
entries.identity_notes: TRPO's constrained policy update differs from PPO's clipped surrogate or adaptive penalty variants. It is an optimization procedure, not a trained policy instance.
limitations: The paper distinguishes its theoretical improvement scheme from practical approximations; this record does not guarantee monotonic improvement for every practical update.
Single-path and vine sampling have different access requirements; the latter assumes the ability to restore sampled states.
entries.abstract_interpretation: The abstract separates a theoretically justified scheme from practical TRPO and reports selected control/game experiments. The curated record retains the method and approximation boundary without universal performance claims.

entries.name: Generalized advantage estimation
entries.title: High-Dimensional Continuous Control Using Generalized Advantage Estimation
entries.definition: An advantage-function estimator for policy-gradient learning formed from an exponentially weighted sum of temporal-difference residuals.
entries.mechanism: For value estimate V, residuals r_t + gamma V(s_{t+1}) - V(s_t) are summed forward with weights (gamma lambda)^l; lambda controls the mixture of multi-step advantage estimates.
entries.locator: Section 3, PDF/printed pp. 4–5; equations 16–19 and bias/variance discussion
entries.identity_notes: GAE estimates advantages used in a policy-gradient update; it is not itself a complete policy optimizer and is distinct from estimating the value function with TD(lambda).
limitations: Bias and variance depend on discounting, lambda and value-function accuracy; no unconditional unbiasedness or variance-reduction claim is made.
The source's combined control system also uses trust-region optimization, which is a separate concept.
entries.abstract_interpretation: The paper proposes a weighted advantage estimator to manage policy-gradient variance and bias, combined with trust-region updates in locomotion experiments. The estimator is curated separately from the full experimental system.

entries.name: Deep deterministic policy gradient
entries.title: Continuous control with deep reinforcement learning
entries.definition: An off-policy actor–critic method for continuous control using neural function approximators and deterministic policy gradients.
entries.mechanism: Replay samples train a critic toward bootstrapped targets and update a deterministic actor through the critic's action gradient; slowly updated target actor and critic networks supply the bootstrap targets.
entries.locator: Section 3, PDF/printed pp. 3–4; Algorithm 1, PDF/printed p. 5
entries.identity_notes: DDPG combines deterministic policy gradients with deep actor/critic approximators, replay and target networks. It is distinct from stochastic maximum-entropy SAC and discrete-action DQN.
limitations: Exploration in the original algorithm adds noise to the actor's action; a deterministic actor does not remove the need for exploration.
The source's simulated-control results do not establish universal stability or performance in every continuous-action environment.
entries.abstract_interpretation: The paper adapts DQN-inspired stabilization to a deterministic actor–critic method for continuous actions and reports simulated-control experiments. Only the mechanism and scope are asserted here.

entries.name: Deep Q-network learning
entries.title: Human-level control through deep reinforcement learning
entries.definition: A deep Q-learning method that trains a neural action-value function using replayed transitions and a separate target network.
entries.mechanism: The 2015 procedure samples replay minibatches, regresses action values toward reward-plus-discounted target-network maxima, and periodically copies the learned network into the target network while collecting actions with an epsilon-greedy policy. Terminal transitions use reward-only targets.
entries.locator: Methods, Model architecture and Training algorithm for deep Q-networks; Algorithm 1, PDF pp. 6–7 (unnumbered Methods pages)
entries.identity_notes: This record denotes the 2015 DQN learning procedure, not any arbitrary neural Q-function, one Atari checkpoint, or later Double DQN/Rainbow variants.
limitations: The cited formulation selects among discrete actions; continuous-action maximization is not supplied by this algorithm.
The Atari results are not a general human-level intelligence or universal-control claim, and no benchmark result is curated here.
entries.abstract_interpretation: The paper combines deep action-value approximation with reinforcement learning and evaluates Atari games. Its human-comparison language is task-specific; the record curates the learning mechanism, not a general-intelligence conclusion.

search_scope_notes: The new Nature search result about discovered RL algorithms supplies additional leads, not verified method identities.
Application papers returned by the broad DQN search are discovery context; using an existing algorithm for plasma, robot, drone or quantum control does not itself establish a new AIConcept.
limitations: Four supported distinct methods were found; discovery has not saturated.
Earlier unresolved generative, graph, interpretation, optimization, symbolic and architecture leads remain active.
No benchmark values, universal improvement guarantees or experimental replication are asserted.
Self-curation and self-review; full PDFs and extracted text remain local reading aids rather than redistributed repository artifacts.
